items.title: Another odd rule
items.prose: Take $\mathbb{R}^2$ with the usual addition, but scale by $\lambda(a, b) = (\lambda a, b)$. The second entry is never scaled.
items.question: Which condition fails?

options.why: Check it: $1(a, b) = (a, b)$. It holds.

items.title: The first dependent vector
items.question: Which vector does the linear dependence lemma find first: the first one in the span of those before it?

options.why: $(0, 1)$ is not a multiple of $(1, 2)$. By then $(2, 4)$ has already been found.
$(1, 2)$ is non-zero, so it is not in the span of the empty list.

explain.text: $(1, 2)$ is non-zero, so it stays. $(2, 4) = 2(1, 2)$ lies in the span before it. Removing it leaves $((1, 2), (0, 1))$, which still spans $\mathbb{R}^2$.

items.title: Distributing in a strange space
items.prose: In the positive reals, $x \oplus y = xy$ and $\lambda \odot x = x^{\lambda}$.
items.question: What is $3 \odot (2 \oplus 5)$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Work out $2 \oplus 5 = 2 \times 5$ first, then raise it to the power 3.

byKey.add: You used ordinary addition and scaling: $3(2 + 5)$. Use $\oplus$ and $\odot$.

explain.text: $2 \oplus 5 = 10$, so $3 \odot 10 = 10^3 = 1000$. The other side, $(3 \odot 2) \oplus (3 \odot 5) = 8 \times 125$, is also 1000. That is the distributive law in this space.

items.title: Why it still spans
items.prose: In the exchange proof, step $k$ puts $\mathbf{u}_k$ into a spanning list. Then it removes the first vector that lies in the span of those before it.
items.question: Why does the list still span $V$ after the removal?

options.text: The removed vector is a combination of the vectors before it, so every combination can avoid it.

options.why: Independence decides which vector goes, not whether the span survives.
Length alone does not give spanning. $(\mathbf{e}_1, 2\mathbf{e}_1)$ has length 2 and spans only a line.

options.text: Removing any vector from a spanning list keeps the span.
options.why: Remove $\mathbf{e}_3$ from $(\mathbf{e}_1, \mathbf{e}_2, \mathbf{e}_3)$ and the span drops to a plane.

feedback.correct: Right. That is the second half of the linear dependence lemma.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Ask what the lemma says about the removed vector.

explain.text: The removed vector equals a combination of the vectors before it. Wherever it appears in a combination, substitute that expression. So the span is unchanged.
